transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I lost my temper on a board call. It was over a small question about the facility budget, nothing that should’ve set me off, and I snapped at people. That’s not how I run my company, and it’s not how I treat people.
Has this kind of loss of temper happened to you before?
Not really like that, no. I mean, I can be firm in meetings, but snapping over a small facility budget question—that’s not how I usually handle myself. It caught me off guard.
Have you been feeling more irritable or short-tempered than usual lately?

Yes, I think so. The board call is the thing that made it clear to me—I snapped over a small facility budget question, and that’s not how I usually run things or treat people. It felt out of character.
Have you experienced any significant changes or stressors in your personal or professional life recently?
Yes. About six days ago there was an explosion and fire during a walkthrough. Since then, things have felt… off, and that’s when this all started.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts or feelings that you can't seem to get out of your head since the explosion and fire?

Yes. It comes back when I’m not trying to think about it. I’ll be in the middle of a call, or just looking over numbers, and suddenly the blast and the fire by the loading area are right there in my head, like a bad film I didn’t ask to see.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities since the explosion and fire?

Yes. I’ve been staying away from the new building. And there’s paperwork I need to deal with—the mortgage folder, the safety reports—but I just leave them sitting there. As soon as I reach for them, my stomach drops, so I put it off.
Have you been feeling constantly on edge or easily startled since the explosion and fire?
Yes. Little things set me off now. If a door slams or the printer starts up behind me, I jump like something happened again. It takes me a few minutes before my hands stop shaking.
How long have you been feeling this way since the explosion and fire?
About six days now. It started right after the explosion and fire during the walkthrough, and it’s pretty much been with me since.
Have you experienced any flashbacks to the explosion and fire?

Yes. It happens even when I’m trying to work. I’ll be on a call, or looking over numbers, and all of a sudden the blast and that fire by the loading area just jump back into my head, like a bad film I didn’t ask to watch.
Have you been trying to avoid thinking about the explosion and fire?

Yes. I’ve been staying away from the new building, and I can’t even make myself open the mortgage folder or the safety reports. As soon as I reach for them, my stomach just drops, so I leave them sitting there.
Has your behavior or these feelings been causing problems for you at work or in your relationships with others?

Yes. I’m still working, but I’m not doing it the way I usually do. I keep putting off decisions about the facility, and I’ve been having other people take calls I’d normally handle myself. On a board call I reacted badly, and that made me realize this is starting to affect my judgment and how I’m leading.
Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for the explosion and fire that happened during the walkthrough?

I don’t know. I’ve asked myself that, but I can’t say I feel like I caused it. I just keep thinking maybe I should’ve seen something or asked more questions, but I’m not sure that’s the same as being responsible.
Have you noticed any problems in your personal relationships since the explosion and fire?

Mostly it’s showing up at work, more than at home. I’m still working, but I’m putting off decisions about the facility, and I’m having other people take calls I’d normally handle. After how I reacted on that board call, I could tell it’s starting to affect my judgment and the way I’m leading people.
Have you been experiencing problems in your relationships with family or friends since the explosion and fire?
I haven’t really noticed problems with family or friends, no. I mean, I may be a little quieter, but there hasn’t been any major conflict or anything like that.
Have you lost interest in activities that you normally enjoy since the explosion and fire?

Yes, I think so. Things I’d usually enjoy or that would calm me down—like working through a chess problem, going over my hiking notes, even having dinner with my wife—they just feel flat right now. I know I should be enjoying them, but I can’t really get there.
